target_customer: Mid-size and enterprise companies running production workloads on AWS (later Azure) that pay for automated disaster recovery
problem: Recovering cloud applications after an outage or ransomware needs manual scripts and runbooks that fail when tested. Arpio maps dependencies, replicates infrastructure and automates failover and recovery in minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, sold directly and through AWS Marketplace and resellers

founders.name: Doug Neumann
prior_employers: Bandwidth (led software engineering through its 2017 IPO)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Shaw Terwilliger
founders.background_notes: YC page says he began writing software at 15 and worked at small, medium and large companies. Dealroom (search snippet) says the pair met at Bandwidth; not opened.

competitors.name: CloudEndure (AWS)
competitors.what: Block-level replication for disaster recovery and migration into AWS; later became AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
competitors.funding_then: Acquired by AWS in Jan 2019 for a reported 200M to 250M dollars

technical_complexity.rationale: Must discover and replicate many AWS services and their dependencies (IAM, VPC and others) and orchestrate recovery across regions; deep cloud API knowledge needed.

defensibility.rationale: Breadth of AWS service coverage (41 services, 150+ resources per company materials) takes time to build, but AWS itself offers DR tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AWS did not absorb the orchestration layer; AWS blog now lists Arpio as a partner solution working alongside its native service.

market_need_then: By 2021 many companies had moved production to AWS, and ransomware and outage concerns were rising; native tools covered servers but not the whole application environment. Founders describe an outage at Bandwidth that existing tools could not recover from (Dealroom snippet).

branding.domain_note: Uses arpio.io; company was previously called Carica Labs per Dealroom snippet (not opened).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, direct with a light playful edge: 'Mistakes happen. Never. Lose. Data.' (company site)

rebrands.why: Not sourced; rename reported by Dealroom listing only

brand_strength.rationale: Short distinctive name but no press about the brand itself; known mainly in AWS partner circles.

pivots.to: AWS and Azure disaster recovery, plus Bedrock agent workloads

outcome_analysis: Arpio is active. After YC W21 it raised an $8.2M seed in August 2023 and a $15M Series A in June 2026, added Azure support in March 2026 and lists enterprise customers such as Finnair and Choice Hotels. Founders with infrastructure experience and a hard technical product that AWS partners with rather than copies helped it. No layoffs or sale found.
notes: Funding between 2018 and 2023 not found; Dealroom lists about 10.4M total through the seed (implies roughly 2.2M earlier), unverified. A WRAL TechWire Aug 2023 article also covers the seed but could not be opened (redirect). CloudEndure source is 2019 (pre-batch) and still relevant. Zerto and Druva not sourced for 2021 so not listed. Series A date from company announcement (June 3, 2026); TipRanks says June 5.
